parts.tts: In nineteen sixty-two, laughing shut down fourteen schools.

lines.text: January thirtieth. A girls' boarding school in Kah-shasha, in what is now Tanzania.

parts.tts: January thirtieth. A girls' boarding school in Kah-shasha, in what is now Tanzania.
parts.heard: January 30th, a girls' boarding school in Ka Shasha, in what is now Tanzania.

lines.text: Three students started laughing... and couldn't stop.
It spread to 95 of the school's 159 students. Some attacks lasted hours. Some lasted days.

parts.tts: It spread to ninety-five of the school's one hundred fifty-nine students. Some attacks lasted hours. Some lasted days.
parts.heard: It spread to 95 of the school's 159 students. Some attacks lasted hours, some lasted days.

lines.text: In March, the school had to close.

parts.tts: In March, the school had to close.
parts.heard: In March, the school had to close.

lines.text: It spread to a village where several of the girls lived. 217 people were affected.

parts.tts: It spread to a village where several of the girls lived. two hundred seventeen people were affected.
parts.heard: It spread to a village where several of the girls lived. 217 people were affected.

lines.text: Then more villages. More schools. About 1,000 people in total. 14 schools shut down.

parts.tts: Then more villages. More schools. About one thousand people in total. fourteen schools shut down.
parts.heard: Then, more villages, more schools, about 1,000 people in total, 14 schools shut down.

lines.text: It wasn't funny. The laughing came with crying, fainting and pain. Doctors called it mass hysteria.

parts.tts: It wasn't funny. The laughing came with crying, fainting and pain. Doctors called it mass hysteria.
parts.heard: It wasn't funny. The laughing came with crying, fainting, and pain. Doctors called it mass hysteria.

lines.text: It took about 18 months to finally fade away.
